pr.title: feat(router): support greedy matches with subsequent static components.

summary: This PR adds support for greedy `{.+}`-style capturing params followed by a static path segment (via lookahead assertions) in linear-router, trie-router, and the shared getPattern helper. In trie-router, the queue-depth calculation used to re-insert nodes matched by a greedy capture computes `m[0].match(/\//)?.length` without the `g` flag, so it only ever returns 0 or 1 regardless of how many slashes are actually present in the captured segment. This means captures spanning three or more path components will be requeued at the wrong depth, potentially breaking matching for deeper greedy captures — a case not exercised by the added tests.

findings.rationale: `m[0].match(/\//)?.length ?? 0` is meant to count how many extra path segments the greedy capture consumed, but the regex has no `g` flag, so `.match()` returns only the first match (an array of length 1) whenever at least one '/' is present, regardless of how many slashes actually occur in the captured string. For captures spanning 3+ path components (e.g. `/:first{.+}/a/b/c/:x` matching a 3-segment capture), componentCount will be computed as 1 instead of the real count, causing the node to be requeued at the wrong depth in `curNodesQueue`, which can make the subsequent static/param matching skip or mis-time the node. Only 2-segment capture cases are covered by the new tests (`foo/bar`), so this edge case is untested.
findings.suggestedCheck: Add a trie-router test where the greedy param captures 3+ path segments before a static suffix (e.g. `/:dirs{.+}/file.html` matched against `/a/b/c/file.html`) and confirm it still matches; verify componentCount logic with `(m[0].match(/\//g) || []).length` instead.
